reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 4.6.3.1 Ensure latest version of openssh is installed

audit.command: command -v lslpp >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; v=$(lslpp -Lcq openssh.base.server 2>/dev/null | cut -d: -f3 | cut -d. -f1); [ -n "$v" ] && [ "$v" -ge 9 ] && echo compliant || echo "openssh.base.server major version: $v"

remediation.command: Install OpenSSH version 9.9 (or later), depending on package source. The current version available from IBM via AIX Web Download Pack Programs is 9.9.3015.1000.

title: Ensure sshd access is configured
description: There are several options available to limit which users and group can access the system via SSH. It is recommended that at least one of the following options be leveraged: AllowUsers: o The AllowUsers variable gives the system administrator the option of allowing specific users to ssh into the system. The list consists of space separated user names. Audit: sshd -T must show at least one AllowUsers/AllowGroups/DenyUsers/DenyGroups; review the lists against site policy.
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 4.6.3.4 Ensure sshd access is configured

audit.command: command -v sshd >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; out=$(sshd -T 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; r=compliant; for p in '^(allowusers|allowgroups|denyusers|denygroups)[[:blank:]]+[^[:blank:]]'; do printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eiq -- "$p" || r="not matched: $p"; done; echo "$r"

remediation.command: Edit the /etc/ssh/sshd_config file to set one or more of the parameter above any Match set entries as follows: AllowUsers <userlist> -OR- AllowGroups <grouplist> -OR- DenyUsers <userlist> -OR- DenyGroups <grouplist> Re-cycle the sshd daemon to pick up the configuration changes: stopsrc -s sshd startsrc -s sshd Note: First occurrence of a option takes precedence, Match set statements withstanding.

title: Ensure sshd LogLevel is configured
description: SSH provides several logging levels with varying amounts of verbosity. The DEBUG options are specifically not recommended other than strictly for debugging SSH communications. These levels provide so much data that it is difficult to identify important security information, and may violate the privacy of users. Audit: evaluates the effective configuration from `sshd -T` (Match blocks must be reviewed separately).
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 4.6.3.10 Ensure sshd LogLevel is configured

audit.command: command -v sshd >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; out=$(sshd -T 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; r=compliant; for p in '^loglevel[[:blank:]]+(VERBOSE|INFO)$'; do printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eiq -- "$p" || r="not matched: $p"; done; echo "$r"

remediation.guidance: Edit the /etc/ssh/sshd_config file to set the parameter above any Match set entries as follows: LogLevel VERBOSE - OR - LogLevel INFO Re-cycle the sshd daemon to pick up the configuration changes: stopsrc -s sshd startsrc -s sshd Note: First occurrence of a option takes precedence, Match set statements withstanding.

title: Ensure sshd MaxAuthTries is configured
description: The MaxAuthTries parameter specifies the maximum number of authentication attempts permitted per connection. When the login failure count reaches half the number, error messages will be written to the syslog file detailing the login failure. Setting the MaxAuthTries parameter to a low number will minimize the risk of successful brute force attacks to the SSH server. While the recommended setting is 4, set the number based on site policy. Audit: evaluates the effective configuration from `sshd -T` (Match blocks must be reviewed separately).
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 4.6.3.12 Ensure sshd MaxAuthTries is configured

audit.command: command -v sshd >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; out=$(sshd -T 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; r=compliant; for p in '^maxauthtries[[:blank:]]+[1-4]$'; do printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eiq -- "$p" || r="not matched: $p"; done; echo "$r"

remediation.guidance: Edit the/etc/ssh/sshd_config file to set the parameter as follows:: MaxAuthTries 4 Re-cycle the sshd daemon to pick up the configuration changes: stopsrc -s sshd startsrc -s sshd

title: Ensure sshd PermitUserEnvironment is disabled
description: The PermitUserEnvironment option allows users to present environment options to the SSH daemon. Permitting users the ability to set environment variables through the SSH daemon could potentially allow users to bypass security controls (e.g. setting an execution path that has SSH executing trojan'd programs) Audit: evaluates the effective configuration from `sshd -T` (Match blocks must be reviewed separately).
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 4.6.3.16 Ensure sshd PermitUserEnvironment is disabled

audit.command: command -v sshd >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; out=$(sshd -T 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; r=compliant; for p in '^permituserenvironment[[:blank:]]+no$'; do printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eiq -- "$p" || r="not matched: $p"; done; echo "$r"

remediation.guidance: Edit the /etc/ssh/sshd_config file to set the parameter: PermitUserEnvironment no Re-cycle the sshd daemon to pick up the configuration changes: stopsrc -s sshd startsrc -s sshd

title: Ensure sshd ReKeyLimit is configured
description: This variable specifies the maximum amount of data that may be transmitted before the session key is renegotiated, optionally followed by a maximum amount of time that may pass before the session key is renegotiated. This recommendation is based on the guidelines outlined in Chapter 9 in [RFC4253], i.e. the recommendation is to release/renew Session keys after one hour or after the transfer of one gigabyte (depending on whichever comes first). Audit: evaluates the effective configuration from `sshd -T` (Match blocks must be reviewed separately).
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 4.6.3.17 Ensure sshd ReKeyLimit is configured

audit.command: command -v sshd >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; out=$(sshd -T 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; r=compliant; for p in '^rekeylimit[[:blank:]]+1073741824[[:blank:]]+3600$'; do printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eiq -- "$p" || r="not matched: $p"; done; echo "$r"

remediation.guidance: Edit the /etc/ssh/sshd_config file to set the parameter as follows: RekeyLimit 1G 3600

title: Ensure sshd ClientAliveInterval and ClientAliveCountMax are configured
description: Note: To clarify, the two settings described below are only meant for idle connections from a protocol perspective and are not meant to check if the user is active or not. An idle user does not mean an idle connection. SSH does not and never had, intentionally, the capability to drop idle users. In order to prevent resource exhaustion, appropriate values should be set for both ClientAliveInterval and ClientAliveCountMax. Audit: evaluates the effective configuration from `sshd -T` (Match blocks must be reviewed separately).
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 4.6.3.18 Ensure sshd ClientAliveInterval and ClientAliveCountMax are configured

audit.command: command -v sshd >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; out=$(sshd -T 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; r=compliant; for p in '^clientaliveinterval[[:blank:]]+[1-9][0-9]*$' '^clientalivecountmax[[:blank:]]+[1-9][0-9]*$'; do printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eiq -- "$p" || r="not matched: $p"; done; echo "$r"

remediation.guidance: Edit the /etc/ssh/sshd_config file to set the ClientAliveInterval and ClientAliveCountMax parameters above any Include and Match entries according to site policy. Example: ClientAliveInterval 15 ClientAliveCountMax 3 Note: First occurrence of a option takes precedence, Match set statements withstanding. If Include locations are enabled, used, and order of precedence is understood in your environment, the entry may be created in a file in Include location.

title: Ensure sendmail version information is hidden
description: The recommendation is to change both the default sendmail greeting and HELP output to not display the sendmail version. The sendmail deamon has a history of security vulnerabilities. The recommendation is to change the default sendmail settings that display the sendmail version and other related information. Audit: SmtpGreetingMessage must be set without "Sendmail $b" and /etc/mail/helpfile must exist.
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 4.6.4.1 Ensure sendmail version information is hidden

audit.command: [ -r /etc/mail/sendmail.cf ] || exit 1; l=$(grep -i "^O SmtpGreetingMessage" /etc/mail/sendmail.cf); if [ -z "$l" ]; then echo "SmtpGreetingMessage not set"; else case "$l" in *"Sendmail \$b"*) echo "version disclosed: $l";; *) [ -e /etc/mail/helpfile ] && echo compliant || echo "sendmail helpfile missing";; esac; fi

remediation.command: Create a backup copy of /etc/mail/sendmail.cf: cp -p /etc/mail/sendmail.cf /etc/mail/sendmail.cf.pre_cis Edit: vi /etc/mail/sendmail.cf Replace: O SmtpGreetingMessage=$j Sendmail $b With: O SmtpGreetingMessage=mailerready Ensure Sendmail helpfile exists test -e /etc/mail/helpfile || touch /etc/mail/helpfile

title: Ensure sendmail PrivacyOptions is configured
description: The recommendation is to ensure that PrivacyOptions includes at least three settings: authwarnings (a default) novrfy noexpn The sendmail deamon has a history of security vulnerabilities. The recommendation is to modify default sendmail settings that otherwise may provide information that can be used by an attacker. novrfy: No Verify: do not verify valid email addresses. Audit: automated read-only check derived from the CIS audit procedure; it prints "compliant" when the control is met.
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 4.6.4.2 Ensure sendmail PrivacyOptions is configured

audit.command: out=$(grep -i "^O PrivacyOptions" /etc/mail/sendmail.cf 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; r=compliant; for o in authwarnings novrfy noexpn; do printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -iq "$o" || r="missing PrivacyOption $o"; done; echo "$r"

remediation.command: Edit the /etc/mail/sendmail.cf file and add any missing options to the O PrivacyOptions directive. Example O PrivacyOptions=authwarnings noexpn novrfy NOTE: sendmail.cf supports the use of both the comma and space characters to separate the options.

title: Ensure access to /etc/mail/sendmail.cf is configured
description: The access controls for /etc/mail/sendmail.cf are applied. The /etc/mail/sendmail.cf file is used by the sendmail daemon to determine its default configuration. This file must be protected from unauthorized access and modifications. Audit: compares `ls -ld` mode (this mode or more restrictive), owner and group with the CIS values; ACLs are not evaluated.
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 4.6.4.3 Ensure access to /etc/mail/sendmail.cf is configured

audit.command: r=compliant; for f in /etc/mail/sendmail.cf; do if [ -e "$f" ]; then set -- $(ls -ld "$f"); s=$(printf '%s %s %s\n' "$1" "$3" "$4" | awk -v m='rw-r-----' -v o='root' -v g='system' '{ok=1; for(i=1;i<=9;i++) if(substr(m,i,1)=="-" && substr($1,i+1,1)!="-") ok=0; if(o!="" && $2 !~ ("^(" o ")$")) ok=0; if(g!="" && $3 !~ ("^(" g ")$")) ok=0; print (ok ? "ok" : $0)}'); [ "$s" = ok ] || r="$f: $s"; else r="$f: missing"; fi; done; echo "$r"

remediation.guidance: Set the recommended permissions and ownership on /etc/mail/sendmail.cf: chmod u=rw,g=r,o= /etc/mail/sendmail.cf chown root.system /etc/mail/sendmail.cf trustchk -u /etc/mail/sendmail.cf mode owner group

title: Ensure access to /var/spool/clientmqueue is configured
description: The recommended DAC (discretionary access control) settings for the /var/spool/clientmqueue directory are applied. Queued messages are the messages that have not yet reached their final destination. To ensure the integrity of the messages during storage, the mail queue directory must be secured from unauthorized access. Audit: compares `ls -ld` mode (this mode or more restrictive), owner and group with the CIS values; ACLs are not evaluated.
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 4.6.4.4 Ensure access to /var/spool/clientmqueue is configured

audit.command: r=compliant; for f in /var/spool/clientmqueue/; do if [ -e "$f" ]; then set -- $(ls -ld "$f"); s=$(printf '%s %s %s\n' "$1" "$3" "$4" | awk -v m='rwxrwx---' -v o='smmsp' -v g='smmsp' '{ok=1; for(i=1;i<=9;i++) if(substr(m,i,1)=="-" && substr($1,i+1,1)!="-") ok=0; if(o!="" && $2 !~ ("^(" o ")$")) ok=0; if(g!="" && $3 !~ ("^(" g ")$")) ok=0; print (ok ? "ok" : $0)}'); [ "$s" = ok ] || r="$f: $s"; else r="$f: missing"; fi; done; echo "$r"

remediation.guidance: Set the recommended permissions and ownership on /var/spool/mqueue: chmod ug=rwx,o= /var/spool/clientmqueue chown smmsp.smmsp /var/spool/clientmqueue

title: Ensure access to /var/spool/mqueue is configured
description: The recommended DAC (discretionary access control) settings for the /var/spool/mqueue directory are applied. The sendmail daemon stores its queued mail in the /var/spool/mqueue directory. Queued messages are the messages that have not yet reached their final destination. Audit: compares `ls -ld` mode (this mode or more restrictive), owner and group with the CIS values; ACLs are not evaluated.
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 4.6.4.5 Ensure access to /var/spool/mqueue is configured

audit.command: r=compliant; for f in /var/spool/mqueue/; do if [ -e "$f" ]; then set -- $(ls -ld "$f"); s=$(printf '%s %s %s\n' "$1" "$3" "$4" | awk -v m='rwx------' -v o='root' -v g='system' '{ok=1; for(i=1;i<=9;i++) if(substr(m,i,1)=="-" && substr($1,i+1,1)!="-") ok=0; if(o!="" && $2 !~ ("^(" o ")$")) ok=0; if(g!="" && $3 !~ ("^(" g ")$")) ok=0; print (ok ? "ok" : $0)}'); [ "$s" = ok ] || r="$f: $s"; else r="$f: missing"; fi; done; echo "$r"

remediation.guidance: Set the recommended permissions and ownership on /var/spool/mqueue: chmod u=rwx,go= /var/spool/mqueue chown root /var/spool/mqueue

title: Ensure logindelay is configured
description: Defines the number of seconds delay between each failed login attempt. This works as a multiplier, so if the parameter is set to 10, after the first failed login it would delay for 10 seconds, after the second failed login 20 seconds etc. In setting the logindelay attribute, this implements a delay multiplier in-between unsuccessful login attempts. Audit: reads `lssec -f /etc/security/login.cfg -s default -a logindelay`.
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 4.7.2 Ensure logindelay is configured

audit.command: command -v lssec >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; out=$(lssec -f /etc/security/login.cfg -s default -a logindelay 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; v=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/.*logindelay=\([^ ]*\).*/\1/p'); if [ -n "$v" ] && [ "$v" -ge 10 ]; then echo compliant; else echo "logindelay=$v"; fi

remediation.command: chsec -f /etc/security/login.cfg -s default -a logindelay=10

title: Ensure loginretries is configured
description: Defines the number of attempts a user has to login to the system before their account is disabled. In setting the loginretries attribute, this ensures that a user can have a pre-defined number of attempts to get their password right, prior to locking the account. Audit: default loginretries must be 5 (1-5 accepted; 0 disables lockout).
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 4.7.3 Ensure loginretries is configured

audit.command: command -v lssec >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; out=$(lssec -f /etc/security/user -s default -a loginretries 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; v=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/.*loginretries=\([^ ]*\).*/\1/p'); if [ -n "$v" ] && [ "$v" -ge 1 ] && [ "$v" -le 5 ]; then echo compliant; else echo "loginretries=$v"; fi

remediation.command: chsec -f /etc/security/user -s default -a loginretries=5

title: Ensure logintimeout is configured
description: Defines the number of seconds during which the password must be typed at login. In setting the logintimeout attribute, a password must be entered within a specified time period. Audit: reads `lssec -f /etc/security/login.cfg -s usw -a logintimeout`.
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 4.7.4 Ensure logintimeout is configured

audit.command: command -v lssec >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; out=$(lssec -f /etc/security/login.cfg -s usw -a logintimeout 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; v=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/.*logintimeout=\([^ ]*\).*/\1/p'); if [ -n "$v" ] && [ "$v" -ge 1 ] && [ "$v" -le 30 ]; then echo compliant; else echo "logintimeout=$v"; fi

remediation.command: chsec -f /etc/security/login.cfg -s usw -a logintimeout=30

title: Ensure TMOUT is configured
description: TMOUT and TIMEOUT are environmental setting that activate the timeout of a shell. The value is in seconds. TMOUT=n - Sets the shell timeout to n seconds. A setting of TMOUT=0, or unset TMOUT disables the automatic session timeout. readonly TMOUT- Both export and lock TMOUT environmental variable to it's present value, preventing unwanted modification during run-time. Audit: /etc/profile must set TMOUT and TIMEOUT to 1-900 seconds and export them (the CIS `readonly` check needs a login shell).
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 4.7.5 Ensure TMOUT is configured

audit.command: [ -r /etc/profile ] || exit 1; t=$(sed -n "s/^[[:blank:]]*TMOUT=\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p" /etc/profile | tail -n 1); u=$(sed -n "s/^[[:blank:]]*TIMEOUT=\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p" /etc/profile | tail -n 1); if [ -n "$t" ] && [ "$t" -ge 1 ] && [ "$t" -le 900 ] && [ -n "$u" ] && [ "$u" -ge 1 ] && [ "$u" -le 900 ] && grep -Eq "^[[:blank:]]*(export|readonly)[[:blank:]].*TMOUT" /etc/profile; then echo compliant; else echo "TMOUT=$t TIMEOUT=$u"; fi

remediation.command: Review /etc/profile to verify that TMOUT and TIMEOUT are configured to: include a timeout of no more than 900 seconds to be readonly verify readonly statement is the last statement /usr/bin/egrep -e "TMOUT|TIMEOUT" /etc/profile This should return something similar to: # TMOUT=120 TMOUT=900 TIMEOUT=900 readonly TMOUT TIMEOUT If either setting is missing, and/or the readonly statement, add these to /etc/profile.

title: Unattended terminal session timeout is 900 seconds (or less) - readonly
description: TMOUT and TIMEOUT are environmental settings that activate the timeout of a shell. readonly TMOUT both exports and locks the variable, preventing unwanted modification during run-time. All systems are vulnerable if terminals are left logged in and unattended. Audit: /etc/profile must set TMOUT and TIMEOUT to 1-900 seconds and mark them readonly.
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 4.7.6 Unattended terminal session timeout is 900 seconds (or less) - readonly

audit.command: [ -r /etc/profile ] || exit 1; t=$(sed -n "s/^[[:blank:]]*TMOUT=\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p" /etc/profile | tail -n 1); u=$(sed -n "s/^[[:blank:]]*TIMEOUT=\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p" /etc/profile | tail -n 1); if [ -n "$t" ] && [ "$t" -ge 1 ] && [ "$t" -le 900 ] && [ -n "$u" ] && [ "$u" -ge 1 ] && [ "$u" -le 900 ] && grep -Eq "^[[:blank:]]*(readonly)[[:blank:]].*TMOUT" /etc/profile; then echo compliant; else echo "TMOUT=$t TIMEOUT=$u"; fi

remediation.command: Review /etc/profile to verify that TMOUT and TIMEOUT are configured to no more than 900 seconds and are readonly, with the readonly statement last: TMOUT=900 TIMEOUT=900 readonly TMOUT TIMEOUT

title: Ensure core dumps are disabled
description: This change disables core dumps in the default user stanza of /etc/security/limits and also ensures the fullcore kernel parameter is set to false. The creation of core dumps can reveal pertinent system information, potentially even passwords, within the core file. The ability to create a core dump is also a vulnerability to be exploited by a hacker. Audit: automated read-only check derived from the CIS audit procedure; it prints "compliant" when the control is met.
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 4.8.3 Ensure core dumps are disabled

audit.command: command -v lssec >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; command -v lsattr >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; a=$(lssec -f /etc/security/limits -s default -a core -a core_hard 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; b=$(lsattr -El sys0 -a fullcore -F value 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; [ "$a" = "default core=0 core_hard=0" ] && [ "$b" = false ] && echo compliant || echo "$a fullcore=$b"

remediation.command: chsec -f /etc/security/limits -s default -a core=0 -a core_hard=0; chdev -l sys0 -a fullcore=false

title: Ensure default path does not include current working directory
description: This change removes any "." or "::" entries from /etc/environment. If a "." or "::" is present the current working directory is included in the default search path. Any "." and "::" will be removed from /etc/environment. This means that any harmful programs placed in common PATH locations, would never be automatically executed. All directories must be explicitly defined within the PATH variable. Audit: automated read-only check derived from the CIS audit procedure; it prints "compliant" when the control is met.
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 4.8.4 Ensure default path does not include current working directory

audit.command: command -v grep >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; [ -r /etc/environment ] || exit 1; out=$( { grep "^PATH=" /etc/environment | sed "s/^PATH=//" | awk '/(^:)|(::)|(:$)|(^\.:)|(:\.:)|(:\.$)|(^\.$)/' ; } 2>/dev/null ); [ -z "$out" ] && echo compliant || printf '%s\n' "$out" | head -n 20

remediation.command: Examine PATH in /etc/environment to see if it contains any "." or "::" entries: grep "^PATH=" /etc/environment |awk '/((:[ \t]*:)|(:[ \t]*$)|(^[\t]*:)|(^.:)|(:.$)|(:.:))/' If the command above yields output, remove the "." and "::" entries from: vi /etc/environment

title: Ensure Address space layout randomization is enabled
description: Address space layout randomization (ASLR) is an exploit mitigation technique which randomly arranges the address space of key data areas of a process. The recommendations here are focused on a system level rather than enterprise. The controls mention both user and administrator accounts. For the purpose of this benchmark, and account is administrator when the AIX user attribute admin is true. Audit: automated read-only check derived from the CIS audit procedure; it prints "compliant" when the control is met.
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 4.9.1 Ensure Address space layout randomization is enabled

audit.command: command -v vmo >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; out=$(vmo -aF 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; r=compliant; for p in '^[[:blank:]]*aslr[[:blank:]]*=[[:blank:]]*2$' '^[[:blank:]]*aslr32[[:blank:]]*=[[:blank:]]*"?0"?$' '^[[:blank:]]*aslr64[[:blank:]]*=[[:blank:]]*"?0"?$' '^[[:blank:]]*aslr32r[[:blank:]]*=[[:blank:]]*333$' '^[[:blank:]]*aslr64r[[:blank:]]*=[[:blank:]]*33333$' '^[[:blank:]]*aslr_r[[:blank:]]*=[[:blank:]]*0$'; do printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq -- "$p" || r="missing: $p"; done; echo "$r"

remediation.command: Run the following command to enable ASLR for all programs: # /usr/sbin/vmo -r -o aslr=2 -o aslr32=0 -o aslr32r=333 -o aslr64=0 -o aslr64r=33333 -o alsr_r=0 A reboot is required before this change takes effect.

title: Ensure usernames and UIDs are unique
description: All users should have a unique UID. In particular the only user on the system to have a UID of 0 should be the root user. Likewise, usernames need to be verified as unique. The only user with a UID of 0 on the system must be the root account. Any account (username) with a UID of 0 has super user privileges on the system and becomes root at login. Access to the root account should be via su, sudo or PKI fingerprint. Audit: automated read-only check derived from the CIS audit procedure; it prints "compliant" when the control is met.
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 5.1.2 Ensure usernames and UIDs are unique

audit.command: command -v cut >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; out=$( { cut -d: -f3 /etc/passwd | sort -n | uniq -d; cut -d: -f1 /etc/passwd | sort | uniq -d ; } 2>/dev/null ); [ -z "$out" ] && echo compliant || printf '%s\n' "$out" | head -n 20

remediation.command: Examine the user IDs of all configured accounts: cut -d: -f 3 /etc/passwd | sort -n | uniq -d If a number, or numbers are returned from the command above, these are UID values which are not unique within the /etc/passwd file. Determine the effected accounts/s: cut -d: -f 1 /etc/passwd | sort -n | uniq -d | while read UID; do cut -f "1 3" -d : /etc/passwd |grep ":${UID}" done Examine the usernames IDs of all configured accounts: cut -d: -f 1 /etc/passwd | sort -n | uniq -d If a username, or usernames are returned from the command above, these are username values which are not unique within the /etc/passwd file. Determine the effected accounts/s: cut -d: -f 1 /etc/passwd | sort -n | uniq -d | while read username; do cut -f "1 3" -d : /etc/passwd |grep "${username}:" done NOTE: Any account names returned should either be deleted or have the UID changed To remove: rmuser <username> To change the UID: chuser id=<id> <username>

title: Ensure group names and GIDs are unique
description: All groups should have a unique GID on the system. All groups should have an individual and unique GID. If GID numbers are shared this could lead to undesirable file and directory access. Audit: automated read-only check derived from the CIS audit procedure; it prints "compliant" when the control is met.
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 5.1.3 Ensure group names and GIDs are unique

audit.command: command -v cut >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; out=$( { cut -d: -f1,3 /etc/group | sort -u | cut -d: -f2 | sort -n | uniq -d; cut -d: -f1,3 /etc/group | sort -u | cut -d: -f1 | sort | uniq -d ; } 2>/dev/null ); [ -z "$out" ] && echo compliant || printf '%s\n' "$out" | head -n 20

remediation.command: Examine the group IDs (GID) of all locally configured accounts: cut -d: -f "1 3" /etc/group | sort -u | cut -d: -f 2 | sort -n | uniq -d If the command has output there is at least one duplicate GID number. Determine any duplicates within the /etc/group file: cut -d: -f "1 3" /etc/group | sort -u | cut -d: -f 2 | sort -n | uniq -d | while read GID; do cut -f "1 3 4" -d : /etc/group | /usr/bin/sort -t: -k2n | grep ":${GID}:" done Examine the names of all locally configured groups: cut -d: -f "1 3" /etc/group | sort -u | cut -d: -f 1 | sort | uniq -d If the command has output there is at least one duplicate group name. Determine any duplicates within the /etc/group file: cut -d: -f "1 3" /etc/group | sort -u | cut -d: -f 1 | sort | uniq -d | while read groupname; do cut -f "1 3 4" -d : /etc/group | /usr/bin/sort -t: -k2n | grep "${groupname}:" done NOTE: Any duplicates returned should either be deleted or have the GID changed. Be careful. We recommend you examine any accounts assigned to a duplicate and ensure the account is neither losing nor gaining authorized group access through any remedial action. title: Ensure user adm is secured
description: This change locks and disables login access for the adm user account. This change disables direct local and remote login to the adm user account. Audit: `lsuser -a account_locked login rlogin adm` must show true/false/false; an absent account is compliant.

title: Ensure access to crontab is configured
description: crontab is the program used to install, deinstall, list or execute the tables used to drive the cron daemon. Each user can have their own crontab, and though files are created, they are not intended to be edited directly. If the /var/adm/cron/cron.allow file exists, then you must be listed (one user per line) therein in order to be allowed to use this command. Audit: cron.deny must not exist and cron.allow must exist (review its users).
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 6.2.2 Ensure access to crontab is configured

audit.command: [ ! -e /var/adm/cron/cron.deny ] && [ -f /var/adm/cron/cron.allow ] && echo compliant || echo "cron.deny present or cron.allow missing"

remediation.guidance: Remove /var/adm/cron/cron.deny if it exists: # /usr/bin/rm /var/adm/cron/cron.deny IF /var/adm/cron/cron.allow does not exist, create the file: # print "root\nadm" > /var/adm/cron/cron.allow IF /var/adm/cron/cron.allow already exists, ensure that it contains at least the root and adm users.

title: Ensure /audit filesystem has been created and configured
description: This recommendation provides guidance for preparing an AIX system to operate with AUDIT active. AIX Audit has been available as part of the kernel since 1995. The historical setup has all of it's files in the root partition. This presents a risk that / (/dev/hd4) may be (nearly) full and impact system availability. Audit: checks the /audit filesystem, mkuser.default auditclasses, the cronaudit job and the inittab audit entry; review /etc/security/audit/config manually.
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 8.1.1 Ensure /audit filesystem has been created and configured

audit.command: command -v lsfs >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; command -v lssec >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; command -v lsitab >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; r=compliant; lsfs /audit >/dev/null 2>&1 || r="Audit Filesystem is missing"; a=$(lssec -f /usr/lib/security/mkuser.default -s user -a auditclasses 2>/dev/null); [ "$a" = "user auditclasses=general,SRC,cron,tcpip" ] || r="mkuser.default: $a"; crontab -l 2>/dev/null | grep -q cronaudit || r="cronaudit cron job missing"; lsitab audit >/dev/null 2>&1 || r="audit inittab entry missing"; echo "$r"

remediation.command: Configure AIX auditing in-line with the High Level AIX Security Expert policy. Create a /audit filesystem, at least 100 MB in size: mklv -y <LV name> -t jfs2 -u 1 -c 1 rootvg 1 hdisk0 crfs -v jfs2 -d <LV name> -m /audit -A yes -t no mount /audit Reflect the following configuration in the /etc/security/audit/config file: vi /etc/security/audit/config Add in: start: binmode = on streammode = off bin: trail = /audit/trail bin1 = /audit/bin1 bin2 = /audit/bin2 binsize = 10240 cmds = /etc/security/audit/bincmds Add the auditing entries for root and all other users below the pre-defined audit classes: users: root = general,SRC,mail,cron,tcpip,ipsec,lvm <user 1> = general,SRC,cron,tcpip <user 2> = general,SRC,cron,tcpip etc. Update the /usr/lib/security/mkuser.default auditclasses entry to ensure that auditing is set up for any newly created users: chsec -f /usr/lib/security/mkuser.default -s user -a auditclasses=general,SRC,cron,tcpip A cron job is implemented to monitor the free space in /audit, running hourly, to ensure that /audit does not fill up. If /audit is greater than 90% used, /audit/trail is moved to /audit/trailOneLevelBack: crontab -e Add in: 0 * ... (see CIS section 8.1.1)

title: Ensure modification to TE system is audited
description: At Level 1, Trusted Execution (TE) should be actively monitoring for applications not yet allowlisted. The recommendation for this is in section two. Additionally, the AIX AUDIT system needs to be configured for modifications to the TE subsystem. Modification to security mechanisms need to be monitored to maintain system integrity. Audit: automated read-only check derived from the CIS audit procedure; it prints "compliant" when the control is met.
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 8.1.3 Ensure modification to TE system is audited

audit.command: out=$(grep -E "^[[:blank:]]*default[[:blank:]]*=" /etc/security/audit/config 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; r=compliant; for p in '(=|,)[[:blank:]]*TE_Untrusted([[:blank:]]*,|[[:blank:]]*$)' '(=|,)[[:blank:]]*TE_FileWrite([[:blank:]]*,|[[:blank:]]*$)' '(=|,)[[:blank:]]*TE_Policies([[:blank:]]*,|[[:blank:]]*$)' '(=|,)[[:blank:]]*TEAdd_Stnz([[:blank:]]*,|[[:blank:]]*$)' '(=|,)[[:blank:]]*TEDel_Stnz([[:blank:]]*,|[[:blank:]]*$)' '(=|,)[[:blank:]]*TESwitch_algo([[:blank:]]*,|[[:blank:]]*$)' '(=|,)[[:blank:]]*TEQuery_Stnz([[:blank:]]*,|[[:blank:]]*$)'; do printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq -- "$p" || r="missing: $p"; done; echo "$r"

remediation.command: Ensure AUDIT Trusted Execution events are in the class default. 1. Edit the file /etc/security/audit/config 2. Find the stanza named classes: 3. If the class default does not exist add a line with: default = TE_Untrusted,TE_FileWrite,TE_Policies,TEAdd_Stnz,TEDel_Stnz,TESwitch_algo,TEQ uery_Stnz 4. If the class default already exists ensure the following audit events are included in the class definition TE_Untrusted,TE_FileWrite,TE_Policies,TEAdd_Stnz,TEDel_Stnz,TESwitch_algo,TEQ uery_Stnz

title: Ensure syslog local logging is configured
description: This recommendation implements a local syslog configuration. Establishing a logging process via syslog provides system and security administrators with pertinent information relating to: login, mail, daemon, user and kernel activity. Audit: /etc/syslog.conf must log auth.info and *.info to local files (verify rotation/archive settings).
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 8.2.1 Ensure syslog local logging is configured

audit.command: out=$(grep -Ev "^[[:blank:]]*(#|$)" /etc/syslog.conf 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; r=compliant; printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "(^|;)auth\.info[[:blank:]]+/" || r="auth.info not logged locally"; printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "^\*\.info[^[:blank:]]*[[:blank:]]+/" || r="*.info not logged locally"; echo "$r"

remediation.command: If not already present, explicitly define a log file for the auth.info output in /etc/syslog.conf: printf "auth.info\t\t/var/log/syslog/auth.log rotate time 1d files 30 compress\n" >> /etc/syslog.conf NOTE: This ensures that remote login, sudo or su attempts are logged separately Create the authlog file and make it readable by root only: # /usr/bin/touch /var/log/syslog/auth.log # /usr/bin/chown root:system /var/log/syslog/auth.log # /usr/bin/chmod u=rw,go= /var/log/syslog/auth.log If not already present, create an entry in /etc/syslog.conf to capture all other output of level info or higher, excluding authentication information, as this is to be captured within /var/log/syslog/info.log: printf "*.info;auth.none\t/var/log/syslog/info.log rotate time 1d files 30 compress\n" >> /etc/syslog.conf Create the syslog file: # /usr/bin/touch /var/log/syslog/info.log # /usr/bin/chown root:system /var/log/syslog/info.log # /usr/bin/chmod u=rw,g=r,o= /var/log/syslog/info.log Refresh syslogd to force the daemon to read the edited /etc/syslog.conf: # refresh -s syslogd

title: Ensure syslog is configured to send logs to a remote log host
description: This recommendation implements a remote syslog configuration. To further enhance the local syslog logging process CIS recommends that syslog information, in particular that generated by the auth facility, is logged remotely. This recommendation assumes that a remote and secure syslog server is available on the network. Audit: automated read-only check derived from the CIS audit procedure; it prints "compliant" when the control is met.
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 8.2.2 Ensure syslog is configured to send logs to a remote log host

audit.command: [ -r /etc/syslog.conf ] || exit 1; n=$(grep -v "^[[:blank:]]*#" /etc/syslog.conf | grep -c "@"); [ "$n" -gt 0 ] && echo compliant || echo "no remote log host"

remediation.command: Explicitly define a remote host for auth.info data in /etc/syslog.conf (enter the remote host IP address in the example below): printf "auth.info\t\t@<IP address of remote syslog server>" >> /etc/syslog.conf NOTE: This ensures that remote login, sudo or su attempts are logged separately Create a remote host entry in /etc/syslog.conf to capture all other output of level info or higher (enter the remote host IP address in the example below): printf "*.info;auth.none\t@<IP address of remote syslog server>\n" >> /etc/syslog.conf Refresh syslogd to force the daemon to read the edited /etc/syslog.conf: refresh -s syslogd

title: Ensure syslog is not configured to receive logs from a remote client
description: 6/27/2025 1.1.0 UPDATED RECOMMENDATION: 5.3.4 - Ensure user guest is secured - Sections Modified: Remediation Procedure 6/27/2025 1.1.0 UPDATED RECOMMENDATION: 5.3.10 - Ensure System Accounts cannot access system using ftp. By default the syslogd daemon accepts all remote syslog messages as no authentication is required. This means that a hacker could flood a server with syslog messages and potentially fill up the /var filesystem. Audit: automated read-only check derived from the CIS audit procedure; it prints "compliant" when the control is met.
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 8.2.3 Ensure syslog is not configured to receive logs from a remote client

audit.command: command -v ps >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; out=$(ps -ef | grep "[/]usr/sbin/syslogd"); case "$out" in *" -r"*) echo compliant;; *) echo "syslogd not running with -r: $out";; esac

remediation.command: If the server does not act as a central syslog server, suppress the logging of messages originating from remote servers: # /usr/bin/chssys -s syslogd -a "-r" Re-cycle syslogd to activate the configuration change: # /usr/bin/stopsrc -s syslogd # /usr/bin/startsrc -s syslogd

title: Ensure system configuration is documented and verified regularly
description: Maintain a listing of the system configuration showing assets configured into the system. All changes to the system configuration should be logged so that the expected configuration is documented. Regular verification of the current configuration makes it possible to identify and correct undocumented system configuration changes. Audit: automated read-only check derived from the CIS audit procedure; it prints "compliant" when the control is met.
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 2.1 Ensure system configuration is documented and verified regularly

audit.command: command -v crontab >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; r=compliant; crontab -l 2>/dev/null | grep -q "/usr/sbin/lsconf -v" || r="missing lsconf -v cron job"; grep -q "syslog/inventory.log " /etc/syslog.conf 2>/dev/null || r="missing syslog/inventory.log entry in /etc/syslog.conf"; echo "$r"

remediation.command: Below may be considered an example of how to setup a regular (daily) verification of the system configuration. The actual frequency you use might differ. The keyword in the recommendation is: regular. Further, the example also shows two syslog reporting lines: one to a system file, the second to a centralized syslog service. The second entry is added as a comment because the hostname is likely not correct and/or there is not a centralized syslog server. The syslog facility local1 is used to keep these reports out of the standard syslog facilities. There is not meant to establish a requirement to use facility local1. An alternate facility can be used as per site policy. Ensure that the log directory and file exist # /usr/bin/mkdir -p /var/log/syslog # /usr/bin/touch /var/log/syslog/inventory.log If logging for local1.info events is not already configured add this to the syslog configuration: #!/usr/bin/ksh /usr/bin/egrep "^local1.info /var/log/syslog/inventory.log" /etc/syslog.conf >/dev/null if [ $? != 0 ]; then print "local1.info /var/log/syslog/inventory.log rotate time 1d files 30 compress" >> /etc/syslog.conf refresh -s syslogd || startsrc -s syslogd ... (see CIS section 2.1)

title: Ensure access on /etc/motd is configured
description: The /etc/motd file contains the message of the day, shown after successful initial login. The /etc/motd file contains the message of the day, shown after successful initial login. The file should only be editable by its owner. Audit: compares `ls -ld` mode (this mode or more restrictive), owner and group with the CIS values; ACLs are not evaluated.
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 4.1.1.4 Ensure access on /etc/motd is configured

audit.command: r=compliant; for f in /etc/motd; do if [ -e "$f" ]; then set -- $(ls -ld "$f"); s=$(printf '%s %s %s\n' "$1" "$3" "$4" | awk -v m='rw-r--r--' -v o='bin' -v g='bin' '{ok=1; for(i=1;i<=9;i++) if(substr(m,i,1)=="-" && substr($1,i+1,1)!="-") ok=0; if(o!="" && $2 !~ ("^(" o ")$")) ok=0; if(g!="" && $3 !~ ("^(" g ")$")) ok=0; print (ok ? "ok" : $0)}'); [ "$s" = ok ] || r="$f: $s"; else r="$f: missing"; fi; done; echo "$r"

remediation.guidance: Apply the appropriate permissions to /etc/motd: chown bin:bin /etc/motd chmod u=rw,go=r /etc/motd

title: Ensure access to /etc/ssh/ssh_banner is configured
description: The contents of the /etc/ssh/ssh_banner file are displayed to users prior to login for connections via SSH. -IF- the /etc/ssh/ssh_banner file does not have the correct access configured, it could be modified by unauthorized users with incorrect or misleading information. Audit: compares `ls -ld` mode (this mode or more restrictive), owner and group with the CIS values; ACLs are not evaluated.
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 4.1.1.7 Ensure access to /etc/ssh/ssh_banner is configured

audit.command: r=compliant; for f in /etc/ssh/ssh_banner; do if [ -e "$f" ]; then set -- $(ls -ld "$f"); s=$(printf '%s %s %s\n' "$1" "$3" "$4" | awk -v m='rw-r--r--' -v o='root' -v g='system' '{ok=1; for(i=1;i<=9;i++) if(substr(m,i,1)=="-" && substr($1,i+1,1)!="-") ok=0; if(o!="" && $2 !~ ("^(" o ")$")) ok=0; if(g!="" && $3 !~ ("^(" g ")$")) ok=0; print (ok ? "ok" : $0)}'); [ "$s" = ok ] || r="$f: $s"; else r="$f: missing"; fi; done; echo "$r"

remediation.guidance: Run the following commands to set mode, owner, and group on /etc/ssh/ssh_banner: # chown root:system /etc/ssh/ssh_banner # chmod u=rw,go=r /etc/ssh/ssh_banner

title: Ensure CDE screensaver lock is enabled
description: The timeout of keyboard and mouse inactivity before a password protected screensaver is invoked by the CDE session manager should be explicitly configured. The default timeout of 30 minutes prior to a password protected screensaver being invoked is too long. The recommendation is to set this to 15 minutes or less to protect from unauthorized access on unattended systems. Audit: compliant when CDE is not installed.
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 4.6.1.7 Ensure CDE screensaver lock is enabled

audit.command: r=compliant; for file in /usr/dt/config/*/sys.resources; do [ -f "$file" ] || continue; e=$(echo "$file" | sed -e s/usr/etc/); if [ ! -f "$e" ]; then r="missing $e"; else grep -q "dtsession\*saverTimeout:" "$e" || r="$e: missing dtsession*saverTimeout"; grep -q "dtsession\*lockTimeout:" "$e" || r="$e: missing dtsession*lockTimeout"; fi; done; echo "$r"

remediation.command: Set the default timeout parameters dtsession*saverTimeout: and dtsession*lockTimeout: for file in /usr/dt/config/*/sys.resources; do etc_file=`echo $file | sed -e s/usr/etc/` echo "\nupdating config file "$etc_file"..." if [[ ! -f $etc_file ]]; then dir=`dirname $file | sed -e s/usr/etc/` mkdir -p $dir cp $file $etc_file fi cp $etc_file $etc_file.bak grep -v 'dtsession\*saverTimeout:' $etc_file > $etc_file.sav grep -v 'dtsession\*lockTimeout:' $etc_file.sav > $etc_file echo 'dtsession*saverTimeout: 15' >> $etc_file echo 'dtsession*lockTimeout: 15' >> $etc_file rm $etc_file.sav done

title: Ensure CDE login screen hostname is masked
description: The Dtlogin*greeting.labelString parameter is the message displayed in the first dialogue box on the CDE login screen. This is where the username is entered. The Dtlogin*greeting.persLabelString is the message displayed in the second dialogue box on the CDE login screen. This is where the password is entered. Audit: compliant when CDE is not installed.
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 4.6.1.8 Ensure CDE login screen hostname is masked

audit.command: r=compliant; for file in /usr/dt/config/*/Xresources; do [ -f "$file" ] || continue; e=$(echo "$file" | sed -e s/usr/etc/); if [ ! -f "$e" ]; then r="missing $e"; else grep -q "Dtlogin\*greeting.labelString:" "$e" || r="$e: missing greeting.labelString"; grep -q "Dtlogin\*greeting.persLabelString:" "$e" || r="$e: missing greeting.persLabelString"; fi; done; echo "$r"

remediation.command: Copy the files from /usr/dt/config/*/Xresources to /etc/dt/config/*/Xresources and add the Dtlogin*greeting.labelString and Dtlogin*greeting.persLabelString parameters to all copied Xresources files: for file in /usr/dt/config/*/Xesources; do etc_file=`echo $file | sed -e s/usr/etc/` echo "\nupdating config file "$etc_file"..." if [[ ! -f $etc_file ]]; then dir=`dirname $file | sed -e s/usr/etc/` mkdir -p $dir cp $file $etc_file fi WARN="Authorized uses only. All activity may be monitored and reported." cp $etc_file $etc_file.bak grep -v 'Dtlogin\*greeting.labelString:' $etc_file > $etc_file.sav grep -v 'Dtlogin\*greeting.persLabelString:' $etc_file.sav > $etc_file echo "Dtlogin*greeting.labelString: $WARN" >> $etc_file echo "Dtlogin*greeting.persLabelString: $WARN" >> $etc_file rm $etc_file.sav done WARN="Authorized uses only. All activity may be monitored and reported." echo "Dtlogin*greeting.labelString: $WARN" >> $dir/Xresources echo "Dtlogin*greeting.persLabelString: $WARN" >> $dir/Xresources done

title: Ensure ftpd login banner is configured
description: Set an ftpd login banner which displays the acceptable usage policy. The message in banner.msg is displayed for FTP logins. Banners display necessary warnings to users trying to gain unauthorized access to the system and are required for legal purposes. The recommendation is to set the banner as: "Authorized uses only. Audit: only evaluated when ftp is enabled in /etc/inetd.conf.
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 4.6.2.2 Ensure ftpd login banner is configured

audit.command: if grep -q "^ftp[[:blank:]]" /etc/inetd.conf 2>/dev/null; then command -v dspcat >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; m=$(dspcat /usr/lib/nls/msg/en_US/ftpd.cat 1 9 2>/dev/null); case "$m" in *"Authorized uses only"*) echo compliant;; *) echo "ftpd banner: $m";; esac; else echo compliant; fi

remediation.command: Ensure that the bos.msg.en_US.net.tcp.client fileset is installed: lslpp -L "bos.msg.en_US.net.tcp.client" NOTE: If the fileset is not installed, install it from the AIX media or another software repository. The fileset should reflect the language used on the server. Once installed set the ftp AUP banner: dspcat -g /usr/lib/nls/msg/en_US/ftpd.cat > /tmp/ftpd.tmp sed "s/\"\%s FTP server (\%s) ready.\"/\"\%s Authorized uses only. All activity may be monitored and reported\"/" /tmp/ftpd.tmp > /tmp/ftpd.msg gencat /usr/lib/nls/msg/en_US/ftpd.cat /tmp/ftpd.msg rm /tmp/ftpd.tmp /tmp/ftpd.msg

title: Ensure sshd Banner is configured
description: The Banner parameter specifies a file whose contents must be sent to the remote user before authentication is permitted. By default, no banner is displayed. Banners are used to warn connecting users of the particular site's policy regarding connection. Presenting a warning message prior to the normal user login may assist the prosecution of trespassers on the computer system. Audit: evaluates the effective configuration from `sshd -T` (Match blocks must be reviewed separately).
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 4.6.3.5 Ensure sshd Banner is configured

audit.command: command -v sshd >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; out=$(sshd -T 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; r=compliant; for p in '^banner[[:blank:]]+/etc/ssh/ssh_banner$'; do printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eiq -- "$p" || r="not matched: $p"; done; echo "$r"

remediation.guidance: Edit the /etc/ssh/sshd_config file to set the parameter above any Match set entries as follows: Banner /etc/ssh/ssh_banner Re-cycle the sshd daemon to pick up the configuration changes: stopsrc -s sshd startsrc -s sshd Note: First occurrence of a option takes precedence, Match set statements withstanding. Edit the file being called by the Banner argument with the appropriate contents according to your site policy.

title: Ensure herald is configured
description: The contents of the herald are displayed to users prior to login for local terminals. Warning messages inform users who are attempting to login to the system of their legal status regarding the system and should include the name of the organization that owns the system and any monitoring policies that are in place. Audit: a default herald must be set in /etc/security/login.cfg (review wording against site policy).
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 4.7.1 Ensure herald is configured

audit.command: command -v lssec >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; out=$(lssec -f /etc/security/login.cfg -s default -a herald 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; v=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/.*herald=\([^ ]*\).*/\1/p'); if [ -n "$v" ]; then echo compliant; else echo "herald=$v"; fi

remediation.command: Add a default login herald to /etc/security/login.cfg with the appropriate contents according to your site policy: chsec -f /etc/security/login.cfg -s default -a herald="Authorized users only. All activity may be monitored and reported.\\nlogin: "

title: Ensure motd is configured
description: Create a /etc/motd file which displays, post initial logon, a statutory warning message. The creation of a /etc/motd file which contains a statutory warning message could aid in the prosecution of offenders guilty of unauthorized system access. Audit: compares `ls -ld` mode (this mode or more restrictive), owner and group with the CIS values; ACLs are not evaluated.
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 4.8.6 Ensure motd is configured

audit.command: r=compliant; for f in /etc/motd; do if [ -e "$f" ]; then set -- $(ls -ld "$f"); s=$(printf '%s %s %s\n' "$1" "$3" "$4" | awk -v m='rw-r--r--' -v o='' -v g='' '{ok=1; for(i=1;i<=9;i++) if(substr(m,i,1)=="-" && substr($1,i+1,1)!="-") ok=0; if(o!="" && $2 !~ ("^(" o ")$")) ok=0; if(g!="" && $3 !~ ("^(" g ")$")) ok=0; print (ok ? "ok" : $0)}'); [ "$s" = ok ] || r="$f: $s"; else r="$f: missing"; fi; done; echo "$r"

remediation.guidance: Create a /etc/motd file: touch /etc/motd chmod u=rw,go=r /etc/motd chown bin:bin /etc/motd Below is a sample banner: *************************************************************************** ` NOTICE TO USERS This computer system is the private property of its owner, whether individual, corporate or government. It is for authorized use only. Users (authorized or unauthorized) have no explicit or implicit expectation of privacy. Any or all uses of this system and all files on this system may be intercepted, monitored, recorded, copied, audited, inspected, and disclosed to your employer, to authorized site, government, and law enforcement personnel, as well as authorized officials of government agencies, both domestic and foreign. By using this system, the user consents to such interception, monitoring,recording, copying, auditing, inspection, and disclosure at the discretion of such personnel or officials. Unauthorized or improper use of this system may result in civil and criminal penalties and administrative or disciplinary action, as appropriate. By continuing to use this system you indicate your awareness of and consent to these terms and ... (see CIS section 4.8.6)

title: Ensure an Inventory of Administrator accounts is established and maintained
description: AIX defines Administrator accounts with the with the attribute admin. When true the account is Administrator and when false the account is considered User. An inventory of accounts with the attribute "admin=true" allows verification that all accounts considered administrative are so labeled by the system.
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 5.1.4 Ensure an Inventory of Administrator accounts is established and maintained

audit.command: Verify that there is, off system, an inventory of Administrative accounts and that the date is not more 13 weeks old.

remediation.command: A printable report can be prepared using the following example: cnt=0 printf "%4s%68s\n" "AIX" "Administator Accounts" lsuser -R files -a admin ALL | while read usr adm; do if [[ ${adm} = "admin=true" ]] ; then printf "%12s" ${usr} let cnt=cnt+1 [[ $(expr ${cnt} % 6) == 0 ]] && print fi done [[ $(expr ${cnt} % 6) != 0 ]] && print

title: Ensure an Inventory of user accounts is established and maintained
description: AIX defines Administrator accounts with the with the attribute admin. When true the account is Administrator and when false the account is considered User. An inventory of accounts with the attribute "admin=true" allows verification that all accounts considered administrative are so labeled by the system.
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 5.1.5 Ensure an Inventory of user accounts is established and maintained

audit.command: Verify that there is, off system, an inventory of User (not Administrative) accounts and that the date is not more 13 weeks old.

remediation.command: A printable report can be prepared using the following example: cnt=0 printf "%4s%68s\n" "AIX" "User Accounts" lsuser -R files -a admin ALL | while read usr adm; do if [[ ${adm} = "admin=false" ]] ; then printf "%12s" ${usr} let cnt=cnt+1 [[ $(expr ${cnt} % 6) == 0 ]] && print fi done [[ $(expr ${cnt} % 6) != 0 ]] && print

title: Ensure Fix Level Recommendation Tool Vulnerability Checker Script (FLRTVC) is regularly checked
description: The Fix Level Recommendation Tool Vulnerability Checker Script (FLRTVC) is a ksh script which uses data from the IBM website to compare the installed filesets and interim fixes on the system against known vulnerabilities and HIPER (High Impact PERvasive) issues. Unpatched software can expose systems to known vulnerabilities that may be exploited by attackers. It is recommended that operating system updates be performed on enterprise assets through automated patch management on a monthly, or more frequent, basis.
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 7.1 Ensure Fix Level Recommendation Tool Vulnerability Checker Script (FLRTVC) is regularly checked

audit.command: 1. Obtain the latest version of FLRTVC from IBM and extract the script to a location on your server. 2. - IF - you are checking an air-gapped server obtain the latest version of fix information from IBM and place in the same directory. 3. Run the following command to check for known vulnerabilities # ./flrtvc.ksh 4. The output should contain similar to the following: # FLRTVC Script executed on Mon Oct 27 13:58:30 GMT 2025 using Version: v0.8.12 # This report is based on APAR file dated : 2025.10.13 Fileset|Current Version|Type|EFix Installed|Abstract|Unsafe ... (full steps: CIS section 7.1)

remediation.command: If any vulnerabilities are reported above, you should review the details from the URL provided in the output before obtaining the fix from IBM support to install on the system.

title: Ensure system firmware updates are installed
description: Security vulnerabilities and functional improvements are regularly addressed through firmware updates to the system and adapter firmware. Unpatched system or adapter firmware can expose systems to known vulnerabilities that may be exploited by attackers. It is recommended that system and adadpter firmware updates be performed on enterprise assets on a regular basis.
reference: CIS IBM AIX 7 Benchmark v1.2.0 - 7.2 Ensure system firmware updates are installed

audit.command: Execute the following command to obtain details of the hardware model and firmware # /usr/sbin/lsconf 2> /dev/null | /usr/bin/grep -E "System Model|Firmware" Compare the installed firmware with the latest available from IBM FixCentral for the identified hardware model. Note: This command should only be run on an partition which has physical hardware adaptors assigned to it. e.g. a partition configured as VIOS.

remediation.command: Download the latest available from IBM FixCentral for the identified hardware model and follow the provided instructions to apply to the system/adapter
